outcome: Transfusion volume (packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelets)
cohort: The study included 42 patients who experienced life-threatening postpartum hemorrhage (>= 5000 mL) at Peking University Third Hospital between January 2010 and December 2019.
finding: Placenta accrete spectrum (PAS) was identified as the most important cause of life-threatening PPH, and the massive transfusion protocol with multidisciplinary cooperation led to a good prognosis for these patients.
mod_finding: The placenta accrete spectrum group had significantly higher rates of previous cesarean sections compared to the uterine atony group.
birth_weight: Average birth weights were 2228.29 ± 840.49 g for the PAS group and 2809.00 ± 500.99 g for the uterine atony group.
gest_age: Average gestational ages were 33.35 ± 3.94 weeks for the PAS group and 37.31 ± 1.93 weeks for the uterine atony group.
